quest.title: Awakening's Real Sound
quest.description: You need the help of the Pari Mihir and Rashnu to obtain the Chaplet. Rashnu seems to be around the giant tree at the Hills of Barsom...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Primogem x50, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

talks.objective: Go to the Hills of Barsom to search for Rashnu

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: That tree... Rashnu is there, but...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: *sigh* Let us draw nearer. I fear that returning Rashnu to the Vourukasha Oasis may not be so easy a thing.

talks.objective: Go to the giant tree to search for Rashnu

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... It's you, Nasejuna! What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: #Ah, honored envoy of Khvarena, and you two... Ah, our Yasnapati and {M#his}{F#her} companion, I suppose?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Gah. Just call us {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: Since I have been given such permission, then allow me to call you by those names... Do you two remember what I mentioned earlier, about how we Skeptics have always been searching for the Kory Drums?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, it was about them being important items for some ritual or something, yeah.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: Well, while I can see that the proper terms were not remembered, that is the essence of the matter, yes.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: The two of you have been acknowledged by Khvarena's Envoy, and yet you know little of our glorious history. I fear that you may be led astray by heresies and heterodoxies from the forest.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: Allow me, then, to explain the true history of Barsom and the Kory Drums.

choices.text: I'll be honest, I'm not so concerned with this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, the stuff Nasejuna says is even harder to understand than the stuff Sorush talks about... Paimon didn't catch any of it the first time...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hmph. In that case, say it more often, Nasejuna, until even one such as Paimon can remember every last word.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Uhh... In that case, let's just hear it once, shall we? {NICKNAME} has a good memory. It'll be fine as long as {M#he}{F#she} remembers.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: ...Long ago, our predecessors worked to quell the disaster that occurred in this land and formed a profound friendship with the Pari.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Barsom's familiar had a preference for music, so we crafted Kory Drums for her. During the ceremony where our bonds with the Pari were made official, five drums had to be gathered and played according to scores.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Though the Kory Drums are long lost, the drum scores have withstood the corrosion of the sandstorms. As you can see, they have been almost perfectly preserved.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Words shall nary describe the true magnificence of that occasion. When the Kory Drums sounded, all things reverberated in unison. It felt as if their sound could freely traverse space and time...

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Those who witnessed it were all shaken to the core. Even the elements themselves were stirred.

choices.text: Sounds like a very lively time.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: *sigh* It's a shame that we Skeptics failed to pass on our legacy, resulting in the loss of all the Kory Drums. And however loudly we cried out, Barsom's familiar would never again utter a word in response.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Barsom's familiar... Is this the Rashnu Sorush mentioned before? Is that who you're talking about? But why wouldn't she respond to the Order of Skeptics' call?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: The Pari and the Order of Skeptics both value tradition and ceremony, so there is routine to our actions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They talk about tradition, but then they lost their drums...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: This is hardly a peaceful land. That such things would happen is little surprise.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mm, okay... Seems like getting Rashnu back to the Vourukasha Oasis with us won't be easy...

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: That is so. We will need to collect all the Kory Drums and play them according to the score...

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Thankfully, I have never once given up searching for the lost drums. I have been gathering the relevant clues even before your arrival.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: As one might have expected of you, Lord Nasuraia.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: There's no need to flatter me. After all, if Aryadeva had not...

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: ...My apologies. I refer to an elder amongst the Order of Skeptics who left for Sumeru City to work on his... light novels, the dratted things. This heavy responsibility would not have fallen to me otherwise.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He became a light novelist?

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: He rambled on and on about how "warring against the Yae Publishing House editor and opponents in Genius Invokation TCG should still be considered war"... But if you ask me, he's just turning into a ridiculous old geezer.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: But he's still an elder who knows more about our heritage than I do, so I have to ask him for information regardless of any... disagreements we might have.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: He's reluctant to answer any questions that don't have to do with light novels and card games, though. It took me three whole questions to receive a single reply...

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Anyway, it took me a great deal of effort just to gather clues about the Kory Drums.

choices.text: I'm getting a headache just thinking about it.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: This is no idle yarn to be told after tea. It is the tale of our meeting with the Pari, the scions of the divine bird, and the long years of war we have endured here in this land thereafter.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, Paimon would prefer "idle yarns," in that case...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yay, new clues! But Nasejuna, if you had the clues all along, why didn't you go look for the lost Kory Drums yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: #That's an easy one to answer. {NICKNAME}, it seems like you're not in possession of a Vision.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's right, I'm not.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: And yet, you're capable of bending the elements to your will... What an enviable gift. Unfortunately, I wasn't blessed with such a gift.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: So it is good that you are here... I mean, we could save quite a lot of trouble for Lady Sorush with your help. Otherwise...

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: I would have to make other arrangements.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: Hahaha, but just as I said before, it seems that even fate is on my side...

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: Lady Sorush, and you two, please, come with me. Hidden treasures may be found closer by than we think.

talks.objective: Go to the location Nasejuna mentioned

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's strange. There's no path here at all! Seems like you're not all that good a guide, Nasejuna.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: There are signs of rockfall...

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: You are observant indeed, honored envoy. I am inclined to think that monster activity caused the rocks to collapse and thus block this... Well, let us call it a path.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: But you may leave this to me, everyone. This problem only requires... a little spark to solve. Ah, yes. For safety concerns, please stand back a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Nasejuna cleans the stone crevice before putting a small package inside. He fills the gap back up, retreats to a safe distance, and lights the fuse.\nThe large rock blocking the way splinters into smaller pieces, and when the dust finally clears, a Gray Gate appears in its wake.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: *cough* Well, that's it for those stones blocking the way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, why's there still a gate in the way?

choices.text: There's always another gate to go through, huh?

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: We used to be able to pass through. As for breaking the seal on this Gray Gate, we will need your help, you two.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, guess that falls to us, huh?

talks.objective: Search for clues in the cavern

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: Regardless, now that we know where the Kory Drums are specifically, we just need to retrieve them all.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: Although the trial here has been destroyed, that may not be the case in other places.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: #Whether they are or not shall be little issue. Let us leave that task to my Yasnapati. This should be no issue to someone of {M#his}{F#her} caliber, no?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course! We're professionals, y'know.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: In that case, you can find the other Kory Drums so long as you follow these notes. I leave that to the two of you. Good luck.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Right, {NICKNAME}, remember to record the drum scores on the stone walls. We'll definitely need them at some point!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, if we take the Dendro Drum here into account, it seems like we've found all five Kory Drums, haven't we? It feels as if we just... happened upon them as we were adventuring.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Convenient things like that do happen every once in a while, I suppose.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: As expected of the Yasnapati whom Lady Sorush acknowledged. This... went faster than I thought it would.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: Have you recorded the entire drum score carved into the stone walls? If you have, let us return to Barsom to begin the ritual.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This place is full of Gray Crystals...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Nasejuna looks around a bit before collecting some scattered records and browsing through them.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: It is not too far from what I expected. The mechanism that sealed the Dendro Drum was once here, but it has been destroyed. There are even some notes here that show where the other Kory Drums might be found.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: As the elders put it, when the Kory Drums were lost in a single night, the Order of Skeptics was overcome with great grief.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: Losing the drums meant losing the bridge that connected them to Barsom's familiar, and from then on, the young were never again able to listen to her teachings — this was a grave incident indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: Great efforts were made by all to search for the drums thereafter, but few gains were made due to the obstruction posed by the defiled energies. According to the elders, this is one of those old locations.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: But as you have seen, those without the power to combat the brute might of the defilement, those who cannot wield the elements, and those who have not obtained the trust of Khvarena's Envoy are unable to reach this place.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: Aryadeva also attempted to retrieve the Dendro Drum here in his youth, but he did not succeed, and has been silent about the matter ever since.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: A sense of responsibility, perhaps... or was it pride that closed his mouth?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y'know, when you said that the Order of Skeptics had a terrible relationship with the Akademiya, Paimon thought that you'd all just stay here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Now that there's that big hole in the sky, never mind not coming back to help out... Don't you think it's kinda weird that he's just over in Sumeru City writing his novels and playing his cards?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Perhaps he can achieve in fantasies what he could not in reality?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean writing the story of his failures into a light novel but changing the ending? ... How's that supposed to solve a real-life problem?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: People need hope in their lives, even if it isn't real.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, Paimon thinks that sticking together is our best chance of fixing this sky-hole problem. It concerns Sorush too, after all!

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Hehe. Your concern, Paimon, is rather wasted on one destined for so grand a sacrifice as I.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Or perhaps I should say that evaluating the choices and fates of others is, itself, an overly prideful act.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon just... just... Ugh, {NICKNAME}, help Paimon out here!

choices.text: We're just here to complete a commission.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Shouldn't we be saying that "we can't just let you be"?

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Forgive my saying so, but such thoughts might be a bit unprofessional for adventurers and specialists.

choices.text: We're to respect their wishes and wish them well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aren't we also supposed to ask them to "leave it to us"?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: I do thank you for your aid, of course, but do not forget. I am the main character of this hymn.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Well if you say so, Sorush, then leave this to us! Just relax, Nasejuna. We know the Kory Drums are very important. {NICKNAME}'s not going to ruin them or anything!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We'll meet there again later.

dialogues.speaker: Rashnu
dialogues.text: Good. Then I shan't have to think about what I should say on the way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Time to look for the other Kory Drums!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see... Next, we just need to put the Kory Drums back in their original places before performing the piece according to the scores on the stone walls, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Rashnu will definitely be happy to answer us when she hears her favorite music.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: Do excuse my presumption, but the ritual that bound the Order of Skeptics to the Pari is one of great significance...

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: I think that it would only be proper Order of Skeptics regulation if its Vijnanapati — that is to say myself — were to preside over it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? But we were the ones who got all the five Kory Drums!

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: Even if you are Lady Sorush's Yasnapati, I believe this to be out of line... or should I call this prideful presumption upon her favor?

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: Lady Sorush is Khvarena's Envoy. She might have behaved more amicably to the two of you on account of your aid in fulfilling her destined mission...

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: Yet this is but a manifestation of her virtue, and not any credit of yours. Do not forget your place. Give praise and stand in awe of her every action, as you should.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, that's what you say... But even though Sorush always acts all high and mighty, Paimon doesn't think she's all that great... or that distant from us.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: That does not sound like something that shall be written into a hymn of praise.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, I'd say it's praise enough by Paimon's standards.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: #Well, what about you, then, {NICKNAME}? Do you desire... Do you want to play the Kory Drums and awaken the familiar of Barsom for me?

choices.text: Eh, Nasejuna can do it. Being a bystander's alright. Sometimes.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Ah, a sensible person, I see. After all, such an important ritual should indeed be left in the hands of one who understands our traditions the most, and who occupies a most suitable position...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Silence! I did tell you before that a Pari's word is final. Doubt not my judgment.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: ...As you will.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, I propose to give you, and no one else, this honorable task. Do you accept?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You need not speak in such a winding manner, Sorush.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #That's right! If you want to ask {NICKNAME} for help, just say "I'll leave it to you" or something. No need for all this weird talk!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: This is not "weird talk." These are words that befit a Pari's stature. Well then. I shall take that as your acquiesence.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well if you say so, Sorush, then leave this to us! Just relax, Nasejuna. We know the Kory Drums are very important. {NICKNAME}'s not going to ruin them or anything!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly. Cooking, combat, errands, espionage, we can do it all! This is definitely way easier than extinguishing the Sign of Apaosha — we're not gonna trip up here!

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: And yet adventurers you remain, rough folk of the outdoors. It would be best if I handle such critical matters related to our history and tradition as this...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: #Nasuraia. {M#He}{F#She} is the Yasnapati I have chosen, and now {M#he}{F#she} willingly serves. Will you bar our path?

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: I... I have no reason to doubt your decisions, astute as they are...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: #Then it is concluded. Speak no more. Come, {NICKNAME}. This momentous task is yours.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't you worry.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Oh, I have no fear. You are my Yasnapati, after all.

choices.text: I've learned many forest tunes from the Aranara.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, and the Aranara sure do love music! And since Rashnu is someone who will respond to humans who call out to her using the music of the Kory Drums, she's definitely a music-loving Pari too, huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Paimon wonders if she'll enjoy Aranara music too...

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: The musical scores of the Kory Drums cannot be compared to some forest ditties! They are part of Order of Skeptics tradition... Perhaps I should be the one to perform instead, rather than let outsiders do it...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: #Nasuraia, you too have merely understood this task from mere writings. The way I see it, would {M#he}{F#she}, experienced in the performing arts as {M#he}{F#she} is, not be the more reliable choice?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The principles are the same. This should be no problem.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: But...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: #No buts. So I have decided, and so it shall be — {NICKNAME} shall do this deed.

talks.objective: Return the Kory Drums to their place

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go together.

dialogues.speaker: Rashnu
dialogues.text: Going together with humans? ... *yawn* Alright.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You return to the Vourukasha Oasis with Rashnu.

dialogues.text: *snore* *snore*

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: Ah! Barsom's familiar has answered our call!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She must be Rashnu. Don't you think she seems kinda... tired, though? Looks like we might need to help her out somehow...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: This is Rashnu indeed, but...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Perhaps we could have a nice meal?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! Grub! Meat, veggies, sweet, salty... Ooh, what should we get? Actually, hang on. Do Pari enjoy human food at all?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Perhaps a repeat performance might do?

dialogues.speaker: Rashnu
dialogues.text: So... noisy... So... sleepy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon kinda thought this might go differently. Y'know, like a moving reunion after many years... Not gonna happen?

dialogues.speaker: Rashnu
dialogues.text: You are Sorush. I recognize you.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: #That's right. This is my Yasnapati, {NICKNAME}, and {M#his}{F#her} companion, Paimon. And that is the Nasuraia of the Order of Skeptics.

dialogues.speaker: Rashnu
dialogues.text: The Skeptics... Yasnapati... *yawn* I do not wish to know... about these human affairs.

dialogues.speaker: Rashnu
dialogues.text: Humans and their drums... are so noisy. I threw them into different places so I could... sleep in peace.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, that wasn't Paimon's fault!

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: How...? But our documents recorded this so very clearly...

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Nor did Lady Sorush say anything against this...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: ...You must have slumbered too long here, Rashnu, muddling your memory of these affairs. Surely the scattering of the Korybantes was meant to select those who might clear the trials...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: With those who could not solve such a small problem proving unfit to call themselves Yasnapati. For how then would they aid me in my great work of extinguishing the Sign of Apaosha?

response.speaker: Rashnu
response.text: The Sign... *sigh* I'm so tired... but this is not the time to sleep.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: #Yes... You see, {NICKNAME} truly deserves the title of "Yasnapati." {M#He}{F#She} has helped me immensely. But {M#his}{F#her} help alone is not enough...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Rashnu, I need yours as well.

response.speaker: Rashnu
response.text: Ah... I get it. It was Zurvan who...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: She, too, approves of me, of course! Alright, Rashnu, will you come with me to the Vourukasha Oasis?

response.speaker: Rashnu
response.text: *yawn* Well, it is not impossible.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Barsom's familiar, please wait. I have many queries regarding the Skeptics' traditions...

response.speaker: Rashnu
response.text: Human business... Later, perhaps. We can talk later. Perhaps after I... sleep for a bit. Maybe then.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Uh...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Nasuraia, do you not have other things to attend to? We can save your business with Rashnu for another day.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: ...Yes. I will return to camp to accomplish... that which I should.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y'know, Paimon kinda feels bad for Nasejuna right now.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm afraid this isn't something we can butt into.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. Nasejuna and Sorush have known each other for a long time... They can settle this stuff between them, can't they?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whatever the case, if you'll come with us to the Vourukasha Oasis, Rashnu, Sorush will be one step closer to getting the Chaplet.

response.speaker: Rashnu
response.text: Together... now?

choices.text: Wait. So this was all a misunderstanding?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well that's one huge misunderstanding, wouldn't you say? Even Paimon doesn't do that.
